title: Completed-to-continuous coefficient verification of Hom localization hypotheses
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-pc-scheme]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $A_X(U)=C(|U|,A)$, the sheaf of continuous $A$-valued functions [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Let $e:B_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$ be the quotient-projection-normalized coefficient identification of [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. Use module sheaves, derived categories and cohomology [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\mathcal C_X\subset D(B_X)$ for the full completed bounded constructible category, including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] along $e^{-1}$ induces an $A$-linear equivalence $T_e:D(B_X)\simeq D(A_X)$ preserving cohomological bounds, integer shifts and coproducts. For $K\in\mathcal C_X$ its image belongs to the same completed integral category under $e$. For every small countable family $(M_i)$ in $D(B_X)$ with a common cohomological lower bound and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, $T_e$ identifies the two shifted-coprojection comparison maps
$$\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(K,M_i[q])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(K,(\bigoplus_iM_i)[q]),\qquad
\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(T_eK,T_eM_i[q])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(T_eK,(\bigoplus_iT_eM_i)[q]),$$
and both are isomorphisms of $A$-modules. The empty family is allowed. Every $L\in\mathcal C_X$ is bounded, hence bounded below, and every $L[q]$ again belongs to $\mathcal C_X$. No flatness or projectivity of the cohomology modules of $L$ is required. No assertion is made for families without a common lower bound.

proof.text: Finite quotient normalization identifies the projections of the inverse image of a continuous constant with those of the completed scalar section. The canonical scalar-to-limit comparison gives its projection equation. The sectionwise inverse-limit universal property identifies these sections. Restriction leaves arrows unchanged, so this equality proves ordinary coefficient linearity. Exact derivation preserves linearity.

Apply derivedRestrictIso_isEquivalence to the inverse coefficient isomorphism. Exact restriction commutes with cohomology and preserves bounds; its faithful ordinary arrow map reflects zero cohomology, hence reflects bounds. Equivalences preserve arbitrary coproduct cocones, including empty ones.

The specified reverse restriction composed with transport is naturally isomorphic to the identity by pbcDerivedRestrictComp and coefficientDerivedRestrictIdentity. The full completion predicate is closed under isomorphism by the uniform-complete triangulated theorem, so round-trip membership retains all witnesses. The stratified perfect characterization gives boundedness and its closure theorem gives all integer shifts.

Apply integralConstructible_hom_sums directly in completed coefficients to K, the countable common-lower-bounded family, the integer shift, and the arbitrary colimit cofan. This proves bijectivity of the completed comparison.

Let c be the unique isomorphism between the transported cofan and the supplied continuous coproduct. Define phi by the linear arrow equivalence followed by commShiftIso, and psi by the same formula followed by c[q]. Shift naturality and the coprojection equations for c give the generator square. DirectSum.linearMap_ext extends it to the direct sums; DirectSum.lmap is bijective because each phi is. Conjugating the completed comparison by this bijection and psi proves bijectivity of the continuous comparison, including the empty family.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q25-e59c2b341 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: There are no new nodes and the statement is unchanged; the 5 steps were read in full against the cited statements. Source: Bhatt–Scholze 1309.1198. Lemma 6.8.2(1) gives O_E,X=lim O_E/ϖ^n (coefficient identification e). Prop 6.8.11(3) gives constructible ⇔ bounded with constructible cohomology. Lemma 6.8.12 gives RHom(K,−) commuting with sums in D^{≥0}; the item limits this to countable families with a common lower bound, matching the hom-sums node and the parent. Step 1: lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor gives the quotient-projection e, which is the same canonical iso as the one hom-sums uses. lem-pur-ring-iso-derived-transport applies with R=B_X, S=A_X, α=e and T=(e^{-1})_*, the right direction. The site is 𝒱-small. A-linearity holds because e preserves constants. Step 2 (elementary): termwise cohomology, shifts and coproduct preservation by an equivalence, empty family included. Step 3: the full statement of lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization ((i)⇔(iii) with witnesses, boundedness, shift closure) gives membership of TK, boundedness and L[q]∈C_X. Its hypotheses are exactly the item's and no flatness is used. Step 4: the hom-sums node in D(A_X) gives exactly the second shifted-coprojection map, with the common lower bound carried over by step 2. Step 5: recomputed ψ(ι_i[q]u)=j_i[q]φ_i(u) by naturality of s and cTι_i=j_i. Edge cases checked: X empty, K=0, empty or singleton family, torsion A/ϖ cohomology, both signs of q. The closures of the cited nodes do not contain the item, so there is no cycle. Batch-5 flag: the ring-iso transport reaches lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective, a Mathlib leaf (Localization.essSurj; Stacks 04VH/04VK) of pure category theory. It is neither the trace formula nor Poincaré duality nor a step of their proofs, so it is genuinely outside the assumptions. The three other-unit tool_uses (ring-iso transport, integral characterization, hom-sums) are generic and accepted. Maintainer note: H^q of the existing lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-bounded-below-compactness would give the D(B_X) Hom clause more directly; the delivered route is correct.
